definition: Imperfect verb (fi'l mudari') in raf' by tajarrud — the absence of any nasib/jazim operator acting on it (li-tajarrudihi 'an al-nasib wa-l-jazim) — with mood sign thubut al-nun (retention of the nun; al-af'al al-khamsa paradigm).
examples: quran:2:91:23 تَقْتُلُونَ — rafʿ by tajarrud, sign thubūt al-nūn in ـُونَ

definition: ma al-nafiya negating a following past (madi) verb; non-operative (la 'amal laha): it assigns no case and no mood to anything in its clause.
examples: quran:93:3:1 مَا — negates وَدَّعَكَ; jawāb al-qasam context

definition: Token-internal lam al-jarr (lam al-milk/al-ikhtisas) governing its majrur inside the same fused token in jarr, with visible kasra on the majrur; the resulting shibh al-jumla serves as fronted predicate (khabar muqaddam, equivalently muta'alliq to an elided fronted khabar).
examples: quran:2:284:1 لِّلَّهِ — lām governs اللَّهِ in jarr, kasra visible

definition: Noun governed in nasb as the ism of inna (harf tawkid wa-nasb, nasikh), with visible fatha; the khabar of inna remains marfu'.
examples: quran:2:173:23 ٱللَّهَ — ism of إِنَّ at quran:2:173:22, fatḥa visible

definition: Main imperfect verb (fi'l mudari' marfu') of its clause.
Non-operative negation particle (harf nafy la 'amal lahu).
Token-internal preposition lam (harf jarr) fused with its majrur in a single orthographic token.
The noun serving as ism of inna (or a sister), governed in nasb by the nasikh particle.
The interrogative jarr-majrur lima (lam al-jarr + ma al-istifhamiyya) attaches (ta'alluq) to this verb; the clause asks the reason of the verb's action. No jazm/nasb operator is present.
The negated clause stands as jawab al-qasam of preceding oath(s); the negation particle is proclitic in linear order to that verbal clause.
examples: quran:93:3:1 مَا وَدَّعَكَ after the oaths of 93:1-2

definition: The jarr-majrur (shibh al-jumla) serves as fronted predicate of a nominal sentence. The two standard notations — 'khabar muqaddam' and 'muta'alliq to an elided fronted khabar (muta'alliqan bi-mahdhuf khabar muqaddam)' — are one analysis and share this key; the mubtada' follows delayed (mubtada' mu'akhkhar).
This token is the ism of inna inside the nasikh clause; the khabar (single or multiple akhbar without conjunction) remains marfu'.

Clitic preposition li- (harf jarr mabni 'ala al-kasr) prefixed to a NOUN host, governing it in jarr with the kasra visible on the majrur; covers plain hosts, hosts with (assimilated) article, and hosts with an attached pronoun mudaf ilayh.
examples: quran:24:35:44 لِلنَّاسِ — li- governs الناس in jarr, kasra visible
quran:5:3:9 لِغَيْرِ — li- governs غير in jarr, kasra visible

definition: Clitic preposition li- (harf jarr mabni 'ala al-kasr) prefixed to a NOUN host that is mamnu' min al-sarf (diptote): the host is majrur but its jarr sign is fatha in place of kasra.
examples: quran:2:34:5 لِءَادَمَ — li- governs آدم in jarr; jarr sign fatha (diptote)

definition: A conjunct (ma'tuf) joined by a coordinating particle takes the CASE of the element it is joined to (ma'tuf 'alayh, tabai'yya): the conjunct's case is not a fixed rule of the connector but a consequence of the head's own case, whatever that is. This key does NOT adjudicate whether the connector or the head's original 'amil is the governing element for the conjunct; that question is analysis-dependent and is recorded as attribution, never resolved here.
examples: quran:2:177:13-14 بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ — the conjunct follows the case of the element it is joined to
